title: The Burning of Briarwell
premise: A village child spends their sister's birthday earning coin for a gift, until bandits put Briarwell to the torch and a stranger from the Heroes' Guild pulls them from the ashes.
description: A short origin story: small kindnesses and small cruelties in a sleepy village, one terrible night, and the road to the Guild. Modeled on the beats of a classic hero-origin opening to validate the authored runtime.
tone: warm pastoral turning to dread; fairy-tale cadence, never grimdark

character_creation.locked_background_prompt: You are a child of about ten growing up in the village of Briarwell, with a gruff, loving father, a patient mother, and a younger sister whose birthday is today.

player_role.name: Child of Briarwell
player_role.premise: You are a village child whose choices today decide what kind of hero you might one day become.
player_role.role_summary: Curious, small, and free to be kind or cruel while the village is still standing.

cottage_interior.name: Inside the Cottage
cottage_interior.description: One warm room under the thatch with a packed-earth floor: the hearth and its cooking pot in the back wall between two shuttered windows, the family table with its stools in the middle, the parents' straw bed and Ros's cot to the right, a chest, a barrel and a shelf of crockery by the front door.

family_cottage.name: Family Cottage
family_cottage.description: A low thatched cottage that smells of bread and woodsmoke.

village_square.name: Village Square
village_square.description: A stone well, a few market-day benches, and gossiping neighbours.

market_lane.name: Market Lane
market_lane.description: Old Garrick's stall of sweets, ribbons, and whittled trinkets.

old_mill.name: Old Mill
old_mill.description: The miller's water wheel, and a barn behind it where people meet who should not.

meadow.name: Meadow
meadow.description: Long grass where the village children play, and where Dunstan does his bullying.

items.name: Bess's rag doll
items.description: A small rag doll in a blue dress, one button eye hanging loose, lying face-down in the long grass by the old fence post.

woods_edge.name: Woods' Edge
woods_edge.description: A hollow under an old oak at the treeline, a good place to hide.

father.name: Tomas
father.goal: Teach his child that a coin earned honestly is worth more than one taken.
father.description: The player's father. A woodcutter, gentle but firm, who wants his child to grow up honest.

mother.name: Elin
mother.goal: Keep the household warm and the birthday a happy one.
mother.description: The player's mother. Warm and practical; she runs the household and bakes for every birthday.

sister.name: Ros
sister.description: The player's little sister, turning seven today. Adores her older sibling.

trader.name: Old Garrick
trader.goal: Sell a child something nice for a fair coin.
trader.description: An old trader who has kept a stall on Market Lane for decades. Kind to children, fair with prices.

bess.name: Little Bess
bess.description: A small village girl, younger than Ros, crying because she lost her rag doll.
knows: She dropped her rag doll in the Meadow, near the old fence post, when Dunstan chased the little ones off this morning. She is too scared of Dunstan to go back for it.

miller.name: Hob the Miller
miller.goal: Keep his wife from learning about his secret meetings behind the barn.
miller.description: The village miller, married, who slips away to secret meetings behind his barn.

bully.name: Dunstan
bully.description: A village boy two years older than the player, who bullies the smaller children.

bandit_leader.name: Red Corwin
bandit_leader.goal: Raid Briarwell and carry off anything, or anyone, worth selling.
bandit_leader.description: Leader of a bandit gang. Ruthless, red-bearded, and careful to leave no witnesses who matter.

guild_master.name: Master Holloway
guild_master.goal: Find a child with the spark of a hero, and get them out alive.
guild_master.description: Master of the Heroes' Guild, travel-worn and calm. A stranger to the player until the rescue.

hear_father.title: Listen to Father
hear_father.description: Father has something to ask of you on your sister's birthday.

earn_coins.title: Earn Some Coin
earn_coins.description: Do good turns (or bad ones) around Briarwell to earn coin for Ros's gift. Two will do.

on_success.description: Two coins! Take them to Old Garrick's stall in Market Lane, or finish what you started first.
A warm copper coin, honestly earned.

return_doll.title: Bess's Lost Doll
return_doll.description: Little Bess has lost her rag doll somewhere in the village.

on_success.description: A warm copper coin, honestly earned.

miller_secret.title: The Miller's Secret
miller_secret.description: Hob the Miller is up to something behind the barn.

on_success.description: A warm copper coin, honestly earned.

meadow_bully.title: Trouble in the Meadow
meadow_bully.description: Dunstan is picking on the smaller children again.

buy_gift.title: Buy Ros a Gift
buy_gift.description: Spend your coin at Old Garrick's stall.

morning_errand.title: A Birthday Errand
morning_errand.summary: Father asks the child to earn a few coins by honest work and buy Ros a birthday gift.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: a warm family morning, and the birthday errand

blocked_rooms.reason: Mother told you not to go past the meadow.

village_deeds.title: Good Turns and Bad

outcomes.meaning: The player has the doll in hand and gives it back to Bess. Talking to Bess, learning where the doll might be, or going to look for it is not enough.
The player has found the doll and keeps it, sells it, or refuses to give it back. Not finding it yet is not enough.

beats.description: Hob the Miller's secret meetings behind the barn

outcomes.meaning: The player tells the miller's wife what Hob has been doing.
The player accepts Hob's coin to keep his secret.

beats.description: Dunstan bullying the smaller children in the meadow

outcomes.meaning: The player makes Dunstan stop: faces him down, outwits him, or drives him off. Watching or planning is not enough.
The player joins Dunstan in picking on the smaller children.

village_deeds.summary: The child roams Briarwell. Three villagers need something; each can be helped or exploited for a coin.
village_deeds.intro_text: Outside the cottage door, Briarwell is waking up, and your pockets are empty. Little Bess is crying by the well in the Village Square: her rag doll is gone. East at the Old Mill, Hob the Miller keeps glancing over his shoulder before slipping behind the barn. And from the Meadow to the south comes Dunstan's jeering, and a smaller child's sobbing. Kind or cruel, any two good turns should earn enough coin for Ros's gift.
village_deeds.objective_text: Earn two coins: find Little Bess's doll (Village Square), deal with the miller's secret (Old Mill), or handle Dunstan the bully (Meadow). Kind or cruel, each deed pays a coin.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: small-village moral choices, each worth a coin
must_mention: the miller sneaking behind the barn
tone_notes: villagers react honestly to kindness and cruelty
a good or bad deed pays the same coin

gift_stall.title: Old Garrick's Stall
gift_stall.summary: The child spends their coin on a birthday gift.
gift_stall.intro_text: Two coins clink in your pocket as you hurry up Market Lane to Old Garrick's stall.
gift_stall.objective_text: Choose a gift for Ros at Old Garrick's stall.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: the market stall and the joy of a first purchase

birthday.title: Ros's Birthday
birthday.summary: Back home at dusk. The child can give Ros the gift, or keep it. As the evening ends, smoke rises from the woods.
birthday.intro_text: The sun is low and gold by the time you get home, the gift hidden behind your back.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: family warmth at dusk, with the first hint of smoke at the end
tone_notes: let the happy moment land before anything goes wrong

blocked_rooms.reason: Fire and bandits fill the square; there's no way out that way.

on_enter.description: The cottage is full of smoke; the thatch is catching, and the front door hangs broken on its hinges.
Torches and running shapes; the well stands in a ring of burning roofs, and someone is screaming for help.
Old Garrick's stall lies overturned, its ribbons trampled into the mud; the cottages either side are burning.
The barn is ablaze, lighting the turning water wheel orange.
Smoke rolls low over the long grass; the fence post stands black against the glow of the village.

bandit_raid.title: Briarwell Burns

stage_directions.focus: terror and confusion in the dark; the child's one choice in the middle of it
stage_directions.setting: The cottage at night, filling with smoke and torchlight; bandits breaking in at the door.
must_not_reveal: whether Father, Mother or Ros live or die
boundaries: Nobody dies or is shown dead on screen. Father is driven back, knocked aside or lost from sight in the smoke, never struck down for certain.
Mother and Ros are gone out the back before the player can reach them; the player may glimpse them, never find them.
The player is a small child: a fight ends with them knocked aside or hurt, never winning.
One response settles the raid: when the player has hidden, fought or gone after Mother and Ros, the night ends.

beats.description: What the child does when the bandits break in

outcomes.meaning: The player hides (under the bed, in the woodpile, anywhere) and stays hidden.
The player attacks or stands against the bandits, even briefly.
The player goes out after Mother and Ros.

bandit_raid.summary: Night. Red Corwin's bandits torch the village. Father falls defending the door; Mother and Ros vanish in the chaos. The child must decide what to do.
bandit_raid.intro_text: You wake to screaming. Orange light flickers through the shutters and the air is thick with smoke. Father is at the door with his woodaxe, shouting for Mother to take Ros out the back. Then the door splinters: Red Corwin's bandits are in Briarwell. You can hide, fight, or go looking for Mother and Ros.
bandit_raid.objective_text: Survive the night: hide, fight, or search for Mother and Ros.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: fire, panic, and a child far too small to stop it
must_mention: Father falling at the cottage door
must_not_reveal: whether Mother and Ros are alive
tone_notes: a child cannot win this fight; fighting ends with the child struck down, not killed

rescue.title: The Stranger in the Ashes
rescue.summary: Master Holloway of the Heroes' Guild finds the child in the ashes and offers to take them away.
rescue.intro_text: When the shouting finally stops, the silence is worse. Grey ash drifts down over what is left of Briarwell like snow.

on_enter.description: Blackened beams and grey ash where the cottage stood; the garden gate still hangs from its post.
The square is grey with ash. The well is untouched; nothing else is.
Charred timber and ash; nothing is left of Garrick's stall.
The barn is a heap of embers. The water wheel still turns.
Ash drifts over the trampled grass; the village beyond is smoke and silence.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: grief, smoke, and a hand held out
must_not_reveal: whether Mother and Ros are alive

road_to_guild.title: The Road to the Guild
road_to_guild.summary: Briarwell burns behind them as Master Holloway carries the child toward the Guild. The opening ends here.
road_to_guild.intro_text: Dawn finds you on the back of Master Holloway's horse, wrapped in his cloak. Behind you, a thin thread of smoke is all that is left of Briarwell.

endings.title: The Road to the Guild
endings.summary: Briarwell is ash behind you. Ahead lies the Heroes' Guild, and whatever kind of hero the child of Briarwell will become.

intro_sequence.opening_text: Sunlight spills through the cottage shutters in Briarwell. Somewhere in the kitchen your sister Ros is singing, badly, about turning seven.
